questions.prompt: A planar 2R arm is exactly stretched out (q2 = 0). What does the rank-deficient Jacobian imply?
options: The arm cannot reach any point, since the workspace collapses to a line
No tip velocity along the arm direction can be produced
The tip position is undefined, so the forward kinematics cannot be evaluated
The joints cannot move at all, since both joint axes are locked
questions.explanation: Both columns point perpendicular to the arm, so no joint motion can move the tip along the arm; the forward kinematics is still defined and the joints can still move.

questions.prompt: For l1 = l2 = 1 and q = (90 deg, 0), what is the entry J11 = -l1 sin(q1) - l2 sin(q1+q2)? Give an integer.
questions.explanation: sin(90 deg) = 1 and sin(90 deg + 0) = 1, so J11 = -1 - 1 = -2.

questions.prompt: A 2R arm has l1 = 0.6 m, l2 = 0.4 m and q2 = 30 degrees. What is det J = l1 l2 sin(q2)? Give 3 decimals.
J = [[-0.6,-0.4],[0.9,0.2]] and the joint rates are (0.5, 0.25) rad/s. What is the x component of the tip velocity in m/s? Give 2 decimals.

questions.skillLabel: Joint torques from a tip force
questions.prompt: With J = [[-0.6,-0.4],[0.9,0.2]] the tip pushes with force F = (3, -2) N. Using tau = J^T F, what is the torque on joint 2 in N m? Give 1 decimal.
A resolved-rate controller drives a 2R arm toward a nearly stretched pose and the commanded joint rates spike. What is the most appropriate fix?
options: Switch to damped least squares (and slow the task near the singularity)
Use the exact matrix inverse with double precision
Use a smaller integration time step only
Increase the joint-rate limits so the commands are accepted
questions.explanation: Damped least squares bounds the rates near singularities at the cost of tracking accuracy. Reducing the time step does not remove the 1/sin(q2) amplification; ignoring the pose is unsafe.

questions.prompt: A central-difference Jacobian check has truncation error proportional to h^2. If the step is reduced from 1e-2 to 1e-3 (and round-off is negligible), by what factor does the error shrink? Give an integer.
questions.explanation: Error ~ h^2, so reducing h by 10 reduces the error by 100.

questions.prompt: Which statement about the pseudoinverse solution qdot = J^+ v is correct?
options: It gives the minimum-norm joint rates for v, but does not enforce limits
It automatically respects joint limits, because the rates are minimal
It never produces large joint rates, even close to a singularity
It avoids collisions with obstacles, because it minimises the motion
questions.explanation: The pseudoinverse minimises joint-rate norm for the task, but it knows nothing about joint limits or obstacles, and it still produces large rates near singularities.

questions.prompt: A 2R arm has l1 = 0.6 m, l2 = 0.4 m and q2 = 30 degrees, so det J = 0.12 m^2. What is the area of the velocity ellipse reached by unit-norm joint rates, pi*|det J|, in m^2/s^2? Give 3 decimals.
A 7-joint arm controls only the 3D position of its hand. What is the dimension of the null space of the 3x7 position Jacobian (assuming full rank)?
questions.explanation: 7 joints minus rank 3 leaves 4 independent self-motions that do not move the hand.

questions.prompt: List three independent tests for a function that returns the Jacobian of a planar arm, and say which kind of bug each catches.
rubric: Compares against a central finite-difference Jacobian at non-trivial joint values (catches wrong derivative terms, swapped rows or columns, angle offsets)
Checks a hand-computed pose such as q = (0, pi/2) and the singular pose q2 = 0 (catches sign errors and checks rank deficiency)
Checks the determinant formula or the shape/linearity J(q) u (catches missing lengths or incorrect dimensions); uses non-zero q1 and unequal link lengths
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.

questions.prompt: Describe how you would monitor and handle singularities in a resolved-rate controller for a 6-joint arm, including what you would log and what the controller does near a singularity.
rubric: Monitors a measure such as the smallest singular value, condition number or manipulability against a threshold
Applies damping (DLS) or slows/stops the task near the threshold, and limits joint rates
Logs the measure and joint rates, and notes that damping trades tracking accuracy for bounded rates
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.

questions.prompt: A planar 3R arm with link lengths (0.7, 0.5, 0.3) m is at q=(0.4, -0.5, 0.9) rad with joint-space mass matrix M=diag(2,1,0.5) kg m². Using the 2×3 position Jacobian, find the joint velocity that gives tip velocity (0.06, 0.09) m/s with minimum kinetic energy ½q̇ᵀMq̇, and give that minimum kinetic energy in joules.
questions.explanation: Minimising ½q̇ᵀMq̇ subject to Jq̇=v gives q̇=M⁻¹Jᵀ(JM⁻¹Jᵀ)⁻¹v. With J=[[-0.4379,-0.1653,-0.2152],[1.3513,0.7065,0.2090]] this is q̇=(0.05485,0.17854,-0.52754) rad/s, and K=½q̇ᵀMq̇=0.08852 J. The unweighted pseudoinverse solution (0.02352,0.23169,-0.50460) has the smaller norm (0.5557 against 0.5596 rad/s) but K=0.09105 J.

questions.skillLabel: Singular set depends on the task point
questions.prompt: A 2R arm has l₁=0.6 m and l₂=0.4 m. The working point of its tool is 0.03 m to the side of link 2's axis, at distance l₂ along it. Using the 2×2 position Jacobian of that point, what is det J (in m²) at the stretched pose q₂=0?
questions.explanation: The point is at the elbow plus R(q₁+q₂)(l₂, w) with w=0.03, so det J = l₁(l₂ sin q₂ + w cos q₂). At q₂=0 this is 0.6·0.03=0.018 m², nonzero: the stretched arm is not singular for this point. The singular poses are q₂=−atan(w/l₂)=−4.29° and 175.71°.

questions.skillLabel: Wrench reference point in τ = Jᵀ F
questions.prompt: A planar 4R arm with unit links has joints at (0,0), (1,0), (2,0), (2,−1) and tip at (3,−1). A tip force f=(5, 2) N acts together with a moment of 4 N m specified about the BASE origin. The columns of your Jacobian are (1; −r_y, r_x) with r the vector from each joint to the tip. Which joint-torque vector (N m) holds the arm in equilibrium?
questions.explanation: The tip-point Jacobian pairs with the moment about the tip: m_tip = m_base − p×f = 4 − (3·2 − (−1)·5) = −7. Then τ_j = −7 + r_j×f with r_j×f = 11, 9, 7, 2, giving (4, 2, 0, −5). Check: τ₁ must equal the total moment about joint 1, 4. Using 4 as if it were about the tip gives (15,13,11,6), the classic wrong answer.
